content: Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) encompasses a broad range of liver conditions, starting from simple fat accumulation in the liver (steatosis) to more severe forms, such as Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis (NASH) and cirrhosis. These advanced stages can potentially progress to hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer). NAFLD is particularly common among adults diagnosed with type 2 diabetes, highlighting a significant overlap between these metabolic conditions. NASH, the progressive and more severe form of NAFLD, has emerged as one of the leading causes of liver transplantation globally. Effectively managing NAFLD in individuals with diabetes necessitates the implementation of targeted therapeutic strategies. This is especially critical given the strong association of NAFLD with increased cardiovascular and metabolic risks, which further complicate the clinical outcomes in this population.
